class_template:rack::history::InverseAct.finding: P2: InverseAction[InverseAction[X]] recurses forever where C++ InverseAction<InverseAction<X>> behaves as X: the outer specialization's _args_InverseAction overrides the inner one (src/rackpy/raw/_componentlibrary.py:91-94), so _run(InverseAction[X], ...) finds InverseAction.undo/redo in the MRO, which call _run again with self._args_InverseAction (still the outer argument), ending in RecursionError (src/rackpy/raw/_history.py:21-29, 43-47). The record's ownership 'value' is also wrong: an InverseAction[T] instance is an action that transfers to Rack on push, like the other action records ('Python's until pushed ...'). Smallest fix: in _run, when klass is an InverseAction specialization, recurse on vars(klass)['_args_InverseAction'][0] with the name swapped; add a nested-specialization test; correct ownership.

field:rack::history::State::actionIndex.finding: P1: unjustified restriction. Rack's State::actionIndex is a public writable int, but State.action_index is read-only (native/bindings/history/history.cpp:590), and the only reason given is 'Rack's own bookkeeping'. Rack misbehaves only for values outside [0, actions.size()], because State::undo/redo/getUndoName index actions[actionIndex] (Rack src/history.cpp). A range-checked setter would keep the public semantics (AGENTS.md: an adapter does not count if public semantics remain inaccessible). Smallest fix: add a setter that checks 0 <= value <= len(actions) and is refused while an action runs; test and document it, or cite an owner-approved contract.

field:rack::history::State::savedIndex.finding: P1: unjustified restriction. Rack's State::savedIndex is a public writable int, and any value is safe in Rack: it is only compared in isSaved and adjusted in push (Rack src/history.cpp). Yet saved_index is read-only (native/bindings/history/history.cpp:592), with no crash, ADR or owner justification. Smallest fix: add a plain setter, test a round-trip together with is_saved(), and document it.

method:rack::history::InverseAction::red.finding: P2: for a nested InverseAction[InverseAction[X]], redo recurses forever (src/rackpy/raw/_history.py:21-29, 46-47 with src/rackpy/raw/_componentlibrary.py:91-94: the outer _args_InverseAction shadows the inner one). For a native T it reaches T._rack_undo -> rackRun, which releases the GIL (native/bindings/history/history.cpp:278-286), yet python.gil_release is false. Callback is null even though Rack calls this Python method through the ActionT trampoline once the action is pushed (history.cpp ActionT::run -> pythonOverride). Smallest fix: resolve the inner specialization's argument in _run, set gil_release to true, and give the record the same 'ui' callback as the other undo/redo records.

method:rack::history::InverseAction::und.finding: P2: for a nested InverseAction[InverseAction[X]], undo recurses forever (src/rackpy/raw/_history.py:21-29, 43-44 with src/rackpy/raw/_componentlibrary.py:91-94). Callback is null even though Rack invokes this Python override via the ActionT trampoline from its history. Smallest fix: resolve the inner specialization's argument in _run, set gil_release to true, and set callback to 'ui'.

record:rack::history::CableRemove.finding: P2: Rack's CableRemove is InverseAction<CableAdd> (history.hpp), but Python's CableRemove derives only from CableAdd (native/bindings/history/history.cpp:546; src/rackpy/raw/history.pyi). Smallest fix: document the divergence, or register CableRemove as a virtual subclass of InverseAction.
